newsitem.title: CONGO: MALI TRADERS LEAVE ZAIRE, FEAR LOOTING IN KINSHASA.
newsitem.headline: MALI TRADERS LEAVE ZAIRE, FEAR LOOTING IN KINSHASA.

text.p: Hundreds of Malian traders fearing an orgy of looting in the Zaire capital Kinshasa brought their wives and children to safety in Congo on Saturday for a privately financed evacuation back to their homeland.
The air bridge from Brazzaville to Bamako, Mali's capital, was organised two weeks ago by Malian industrialist Babani Sisoko and has completed several shuttle flights using chartered aircraft.

"We were looted in '91 and again in '93, wiped out," said one Malian trader who brought his wife and five children across the Zaire River to Brazzaville from Kinshasa. "It's not going to happen again with my family there."
Unrest in Kinshasa has resulted in widespread looting twice in the past seven years.

With the rebel forces of Laurent Kabila closing in on the government of President Mobutu Sese Seko, Malians are leaping at Sisoko's offer of free flights out, if only they can take the ferry to Brazzaville, about a mile away (1.5 km) across the river, formerly the Congo.
Hundreds of Malians, the women in colourful traditional dress, thronged Brazzaville's Maya-Maya airport in the heat of Saturday morning.
"There's no more effective government. I'm afraid they'll clean me out at gunpoint," said one Malian businessman, referring to fears that government troops might pillage the capital.
"Last time, in '93, it was only the Europeans that got out in time," he added.
Ferries docking at Brazzaville's "beach" entryport in the past two days have brought handfuls of non-Africans over to Congo, including some Chinese diplomats who left on Saturday.
